Tehran is taking a significant step to change the status quo and the red lines that uphold it, in line with Mojtaba Khamenei's edict that there has to be either war or peace, but nothing in between.

The status quo pre-midterm was that the US turned a bit of a blind eye to Tehran bypassing the US blockade—via STS.

After the midterms, having rejected military options, Trump ordered an intensification of Bessent's economic warfare, including clamping down on Tehran's use of STS to get its oil out. This also entailed more attacks on Iranian radar and missile sites.

Iran has responded by striking US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, as well as further targeting ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian approval.

That is, Tehran is shifting the fault lines: The blockade is an act of war, and if it is implemented, there will be war, not just occasional strikes. 

Tehran is doing this partly because it has observed Trump's many empty threats and prolonged hesitation to restart the third round of war and concluded that Trump knows that he has no good military options. If, in his mind, good military options existed, Trump would have exercised them by now, Tehran believes.

As a result, the calculation is that Tehran can shift the fault lines through the threat of escalation, i.e., striking GCC oil facilities if Iran cannot sell its oil. 

It's unclear whether this gamble will work, but in my assessment, it increases the likelihood of Trump gravitating toward the Swiss Cheese option I have written about. That is, Trump declares victory, walks away, but in order to make the new status quo somewhat stable and disincentivize Iran from escalating, Trump slowly ceases to implement the blockade and oil sanctions.
